candidates.evidence: Only a weak recollection that Bi2O2Se shows a strong A1g-type mode near 160 cm-1, which resembles the measured 155.7 cm-1 peak. The 299 and 354 cm-1 modes were not checked against any reference, no literature was accessible here, and the match is unverified.

hint_reasoning: No material hint was given (material_hint is null), so there is nothing to verify. I did not identify the material from the working-directory name. The three measured modes do not match any reference I can check in this environment, so I cannot confirm a material from the spectrum.

limits: Identification is not established. Three modes at 155.7, 299.1 and 354.1 cm-1 were measured, but I could not match them to a reference in this environment. The Bi2O2Se candidate is a weak recollection with confidence 0.1 and no supporting data. I did not use the working-directory name as evidence.

Noise is about 220 counts per point against a background of about 1000-2500 counts. Only the three modes above are significant. A weak bump near 147 cm-1 (S/N ~4.5) is a shoulder of the 156 mode, and a two-component fit was not preferred by BIC. Features near 122, 188, 211 and 267 cm-1 are at noise level and were not reported.

No Si substrate line is present. The 505-535 cm-1 window gives a broad bump at 525.8 cm-1 with FWHM 11.7 cm-1 and height 677 counts, which is not a Si line (it should be about 3-4 cm-1 wide at 520.7). Raw means of 2402, 2390 and 2328 counts at 510-530, 480-500 and 540-560 cm-1 show no step. Nothing was reported as Si substrate.
Spectral range is 60-1100 cm-1 only. Modes below 60 cm-1 and above 1100 cm-1 were not measured, so higher-frequency fingerprint modes of a candidate material cannot be checked.

There are no polarization or angle-resolved data, so no symmetry (irrep) or polarization pattern can be assigned. No temperature series was provided, so the 295 K measurement cannot be compared with low-temperature phonon behaviour.
The cosmic-ray spike at 897.47 cm-1 (9238 counts vs neighbours 1696 and 1499) is a single-pixel event and was removed before fitting. It is not a Raman peak.

The broad, decreasing background (about 2800 counts at 60 cm-1 falling to about 1000 at 1100 cm-1) was removed by asymmetric least-squares baseline subtraction. It is most likely fluorescence, and this subtraction may slightly shift the apparent intensities of the broad features.
